what: Rivian makes electric vehicles. It sells the R1T pickup and R1S sport utility vehicle to consumers, builds electric delivery vans, and is preparing the cheaper R2 model. Volkswagen has invested in a joint venture for its software and electrical architecture.
customers: Consumers buying premium electric trucks and sport utility vehicles, and commercial fleets buying delivery vans.
money: the Volkswagen joint venture, charging and service
moat: Its own electrical architecture and software, which Volkswagen paid billions to license, in an area where most traditional carmakers have struggled.
risks: It loses a very large amount per vehicle, with an operating margin around negative 67%
Gross margin of 3% means it barely covers the cost of building each car
Electric vehicle demand growth slowed when US tax credits were withdrawn
It will need more capital if losses continue
opportunities: Cash of about $5.5 billion roughly matches its debt
The R2 is aimed at a far larger market at a much lower price
Analysts see large upside, reflecting the size of the opportunity if R2 succeeds
watch: Gross margin per vehicle and the R2 production launch.
